correctness.rationale: Direct quiver multiplication gives exactly independent per-arrow 2x2 minor constraints after fixing vertex coefficient t-vectors. For a vertex difference of valuation a, an invertible coordinate reduction and the chain-ring annihilator cardinality yield exactly q^{L+(t-1)a} arrow-vector choices, including zero differences. The telescoping valuation expansion and successive quotient filtration give q^{t sum_h c(E_h)} vertex lifts. Orientation and matroid dependence follow from valuations and graph rank. The explicit verifier completed 12 independent literal-product exhaustive cases over Z/p^L and truncated polynomial rings, checking characteristic, loop, orientation, multiplicity, t=1 and t=3 boundaries. These finite checks are corroborative, not the proof.

value.rationale: The number of ordered pairwise commuting tuples in a finite ring algebra is a natural noncommutativity invariant. The theorem completely computes this invariant for every tuple arity and every finite chain-ring length for a general multigraph-indexed algebra, identifies the exact role of graphic-matroid rank, and proves coefficient-ring universality across rings of different characteristic, illustrated by Z/4Z versus F2[ε]/ε². These are structural consequences not implied merely by the standard one-level Potts polynomial; they supply an efficient finite algorithm and a meaningful global classification of invariant dependence.
